specification_compliance: I29: frontend/src/lib/format.ts:21-42 formatRelativeAge returns a relative age at every age; it uses months below 360 days and years from 360 days on, with Math.max(1, floor(days/365)). That makes 360-364 days read '1 year ago' rather than '12 months ago', and it never falls back to a date. frontend/src/components/readingapp/ReadingCard.tsx:71 renders the folder label · formatRelativeAge(created_at, locale).

The boundary table in frontend/src/lib/__tests__/format.test.ts:58-73 is consistent with the code by reading (I did not run it): 359 days gives 11 months, 360 gives 1 year, 729 gives 1 year, and 730 gives 2 years, in en and ja.
potential_unspecified_behavior: For days 360-364, floor(days/365) is 0, and the Math.max(1, ...) clamp turns it into 1 year. This is intended.
Ages use fixed 30- and 365-day buckets, not calendar months, so 30-59 days reads '1 month ago'. This is consistent with existing behavior.
regression_risks: formatRelativeAge has only one caller, ReadingCard.tsx, so Video and Home dates (formatRelativeDate) are not affected.
test_coverage: format.test.ts covers the boundaries of the week, month and year buckets in en and ja with frozen timers. The sub-day branches (seconds, minutes, hours, 'yesterday') are not covered in this table.
